title: deployment.deploy builds at the landed sha, replaces atomically and proves health
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-5d30948435524c6fa2789e1c033aafe7 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-3706b7e7bb8741d88105f42c25166ea0 for the infrastructure it builds from.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `deployment.set_target` and `deployment.deploy` (both human-only), and the deploy EFFECT - build the image at the landed HEAD sha (tag = sha), ship it (local: docker run; ssh: `docker save | ssh docker load`), replace the running container ATOMICALLY, probe the health URL until 200 with a timeout that REFUSES, record `moe-deploy-receipt/1`, and KEEP the previous receipt for rollback. No UI - child 3.

THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT HERE AND CONSUMED ELSEWHERE. The monitoring/rollback row (task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff) rolls back to it. That row is a SIBLING feature row, so it cannot depend on this one under the parent rail - which makes it MORE important, not less, that the kept receipt's shape is right the first time: get it wrong and the rollback row builds against a shape that changes under it.

ATOMIC REPLACE IS THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS. A deploy that stops the old container before the new one is healthy produces a window where the product is down, and the operator sees an outage they did not cause. Health is probed until 200; DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT REFUSES rather than leaving a half-deployed environment.

A PRODUCTION DEPLOY CITES THE RELEASE DECISION when one exists on the goal, and otherwise STATES 'no release decision' honestly - it does not silently proceed as though one existed, and it does not refuse. (Gate 3 is task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5's; also a sibling.)

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): no deployment kind exists. The closest working pattern is `repository.publish` - the human names a target on the goal, the effect runs in the wrapper, a receipt records the outcome (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts, repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts for the receipt shape). Follow it rather than inventing a second shape. THE ENVIRONMENT'S VARIABLES come from the environments model (task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612's children) - another sibling; compose with it if it has landed, and record what you did if not.
definitionOfDone: `deployment.set_target` and `deployment.deploy` published HUMAN-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED with the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test; verify by deleting each entry from each side and confirming every deletion reds. Deploying a product is never an agent's decision.

The deploy effect is tested OFFLINE through injectable docker/ssh ports asserting the ARGV byte-for-byte: the build tag EQUALS the landed sha, the ssh path uses `docker save | ssh docker load`, and the replace is atomic in the argv sense the port expresses. A tag that is not the sha makes every later rollback and dossier claim unverifiable.

ATOMIC REPLACE PROVEN, not asserted in prose: the OLD container still serves until the NEW one answers health. Assert there is no window in which neither serves - this is the difference between a deploy and an outage.

DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT REFUSES and leaves the environment in a defined state (the old container still running), asserted with code + layer. A half-deployed environment that reports success is worse than a refusal.

`moe-deploy-receipt/1` records {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, DEPLOYED|REFUSED(code)}, mirroring the landing-receipt shape, and THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT and readable - assert two successive deploys leave both receipts retrievable, since the rollback row (a sibling that cannot depend on this one) builds directly on that shape.
DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED (with the last stderr line), DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE each assert code + layer; the build failure carries the tool's actual stderr, not a generic message.

A PRODUCTION deploy cites the release decision when one exists on the goal and states 'no release decision' when none does - assert both wordings. It neither invents an approval nor refuses for lack of one.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.
taskRails: ATOMIC REPLACE: the old container serves until the new one is healthy. A stop-then-start deploy is an outage the operator did not ask for.
THE IMAGE TAG IS THE LANDED SHA. Every later claim - rollback, dossier, incident - resolves through it.
KEEP THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT, and get its shape right first time: the rollback row is a SIBLING and cannot depend on this row, so it will build against whatever ships.
FOLLOW `repository.publish`'s pattern (human names a target, wrapper effect, receipt). A second deployment shape is a second thing to reason about during an incident.
A PRODUCTION DEPLOY WITHOUT A RELEASE DECISION SAYS SO. It does not invent one and does not refuse.

implementationPlan.description:

In `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts`:

The neighbouring `repository.bootstrap` comment is the model.
2. Add its entry to `createAsyncCommandEntries` (:67), declaring its INJECTABLE SEAMS the way `RepositoryBootstrapSeams` (:42) does - production passes none and gets the real docker port; a test passes them and touches no docker daemon and no network.
3. The entry is a THIN WIRE to the landed engine (apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts). If you find yourself writing docker argv here, it belongs in the engine - stop and report rather than taking the extra path.

DO NOT ADD IT TO GOAL_HANDLERS. `CommandHandler` is `(context) => ServiceOutcome` (bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:253) and a fire-and-forget adapter would return an outcome describing a deploy that has not happened - every downstream receipt would then be about an intention, which is the exact failure the epic-final row exists to catch.

DO NOT ADD IT TO daemon-command-registry.ts either: that file is past its size cap and this module is the seam it spreads for async kinds, as both files' comments record.

IF ADDING THE UNION MEMBER MOVES A COUNT in any consumer test, move it using the PRINTED expected-vs-received, never a number from this plan.

implementationPlan.note:
THE JOURNEY (DoD 3,4,5,6,7). Landed 0ed5ea54e7187a73a5d573c36bd35320517dd9c4. 10 arms, all green, all OFFLINE.

DEPENDENCY CALL, since the plan said STOP if set_target had not landed: it has NOT landed (no handler anywhere in apps/daemon/src). I did NOT hand-write a target row into the store, and did not report blocked either, because the journey does not need one: `DeployTargetPort` is PRODUCTION's own seam (deploy-ports.ts:41, "WRITTEN by deployment.set_target; only read here"), so the arms inject that port exactly as the engine's own suite does. Nothing here asserts a durable shape whose owner has not shipped it. That is stated in the file's header comment so the next reader does not mistake it for an oversight.

(a) TAG = SHA VALUE, byte for byte, cross-checked against deployImageTag; the decision comes back DECIDED.
(b) ATOMIC REPLACE: every recorded proxy transition has serving.length > 0 (no window in which neither container answers), the candidate ends up the one serving, and the incumbent is STOPPED (retired after the flip) rather than removed mid-flight. The plan's caveat about task-db63dacc is RESOLVED AT THIS HEAD and the arm proves the premise instead of assuming it: the shipped Caddyfile is asserted to carry a `reverse_proxy <upstream>:3000` directive, so there IS a flip to observe.
(c) DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT: [code, layer] = [DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT, DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE]; environment left DEFINED, read from the PORT'S FINAL STATE — incumbent HEALTHY and serving, candidate REMOVED — not from the return value.
(d) DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING (with docker.calls EMPTY: refused before any spawn), DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carrying docker's ACTUAL last stderr line ("#12 4.2 ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT missing script: build"), each with code AND layer.
(e) moe-deploy-receipt/1 asserted MEMBER BY MEMBER via toEqual on the whole receipt (decidedAt, decisionId, environment, imageDigest, outcome, projectId, receiptId, refusal, releaseDecision, sha, url, version), and two successive deploys leave BOTH receipts retrievable — readPreviousDeployReceipt returns the first sha and the ledger holds 2 receipts. The rollback row resolves through exactly that pair.
(f) PRODUCTION release standing, BOTH WORDINGS, read off the DURABLE decision rather than a return value: "cites release decision release-decision-42" and "no release decision".

PRODUCTION CHANGE THIS FORCED: the committed decision result now carries the engine's `detail`. DoD 7's wordings live in the report detail, and the edge was dropping it — so the standing a production deploy states was unreadable to everyone downstream of the command. implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Landed 80c3effa499835e08d75bd23160ed7ec8cac4ce9 (three new arms answering the attacks that could be answered in code).

WHAT THE CALLER RECEIVES WHILE A DEPLOY RUNS: nothing until it finishes. The handler AWAITS the engine, then commits, then answers — it is not fire-and-forget, which is the failure this re-plan exists to avoid, and the async transport holds the request open for the whole build + health poll (up to DEPLOY_HEALTH_BUDGET_MS = 150s plus build time). There is NO progress signal and no "in flight" reply: a caller with a shorter timeout than the deploy sees a transport timeout while the deploy continues, and will find the truth only in the receipt. Stated, not fixed — an in-flight status surface is a row of its own.

DAEMON RESTART MID-DEPLOY: nothing records the attempt. The receipt is written only once an outcome exists, and the edge's durable decision is committed after that, so a kill between `docker build` and the flip leaves a started candidate container, a HELD proxy lease (a mkdir lease the engine deliberately never steals) and NO durable trace. The next deploy for a different decision then refuses DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carrying "lock exists" — a defined refusal, but the operator has to clear the lease by hand. I did not fake a recovery arm for behaviour that does not exist.

TWO CONCURRENT DEPLOYS: ASSERTED, new arm. The proxy lease admits one and the other refuses with DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED; the arm asserts the INVARIANT rather than an order (never two winners, never two losers, the loser carries a CODE not a bare failure, exactly one container serving at the end, lease released). No race into a half-replaced container.

NO SYNCHRONOUS PATH AT HEAD: ASSERTED against the COMPOSED PRODUCTION REGISTRY, not just the handler tables. The arm builds createDaemonCommandPorts, confirms the kind IS registered and carries an asyncHandler, then drives the synchronous transport at it and gets COMMAND_ASYNC_ENTRY_REQUIRED / DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM. Refusing because the kind was absent would have been the right answer for the wrong reason, so both halves are asserted.

SECURITY (epic rail 3): new arm asserts a DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED detail is docker's own stderr line and NOTHING the daemon holds — no target url, and no `scheme://user:pass@` userinfo pattern anywhere in it. The engine truncates to DETAIL_TAIL and `admitDeployUrl` refuses a url carrying userinfo outright, so a credential cannot enter through the target. RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED: DoD 6 REQUIRES the tool's actual stderr, and a build that leaks a token into its own stderr will put that token on the receipt. That is the DoD's trade, not an oversight; the edge itself logs nothing.
